intent: Show a Broomfield homeowner what the city's own 2026 landscape code names for artificial turf — where it's permitted, the city's own contradictory note about whether the new rules touch single-unit homes at all, and the two water rules (Water Use Ordinance, Drought Watch) that a turf lawn sidesteps.
distinctValue: Broomfield is a combined city and county with its own landscape ordinance (No. 2291, adopted 13 January 2026) that names artificial turf directly and limits it to single-unit backyards, athletic fields and purpose-built dog parks — a rule no neighboring published page (Westminster, Superior, Louisville, Erie, Lafayette, Northglenn, Thornton) carries. The city's own explainer also undercuts its own permitted-use list by saying the new regulations don't affect single-unit residential landscaping at all, which this page surfaces as a question for Broomfield Planning rather than asserting either reading as settled.

sources.label: Broomfield Voice: landscape code update (Ordinance No. 2291)
supports: Ordinance 2291: The page confirms this ordinance updates the Broomfield Municipal Code for revised turf requirements and was approved January 13, 2026.
Artificial turf is permitted in specific areas: Athletic fields of play, Backyards of single-unit residential lots, Dog parks (when specifically designed for that use).
The new regulations do not impact landscaping for single-unit residential properties, including both attached and detached homes.
Ordinance No. 2291 Revisions to the Landscape Code for Revised Turf Requirements
Chapter 17-70 relating to turf and other related revisions

sources.label: City of Broomfield: Water Use Ordinance
supports: Water only between 6 p.m. and 10 a.m.
Watering no more than three days per week, even when there is no drought
Repair leaking sprinkler systems within 10 days
Don't let water pool on hard surfaces or flow down gutters
Hard surface cleaning with water only permitted for public health/safety concerns

sources.label: City of Broomfield: Water Use and Drought Levels
supports: residents are asked to voluntarily limit watering to no more than two days per week
